page.layout: One page of text in a single column; running head at top; a catchword "IN" at lower right; no margin notes.

l.i: OVÆ Voce nobis prodidit Deus sua,
Ratione sciri nec queunt humanitus,
Vanis sophorum somnians insomnis
Vel posse nosci, vel doceri certius:
Id est tenebris lucem egere cogitans,
Princeps haberi dignus est amentium.
Mendacium nam veritas coarguit:
Sed veritatem non probat mendacium.
IVrare Numen, Numen est folio in suo
Locare, partim ut abditorum conscium,
Suaque partim ut veritatis vindicem.
Scienter ergo, falsa vel per Numina,
Falsumve iurans, scis quod admittas scelus?
Certè in Dei throno, Dei hostem collocas,
In Veritatis pulpito Mendacium.
Nec huius in caput supera ruetis omnia?
Nec infera huius concidetis sub pedes?
At te, sceleste quolibet scelestior,
Ipsum ore Numen qui lacessis impio,
Ut sceleris unum inexplicabilis reum, Exspectat vni poena nota Numini.

page.notes: Lower-right catchword "IN" is partly cut off. Some letters in the long-s/f forms (e.g. "Vel posse") are doubtful; the Greek-looking "Ꝑ" glyphs read as v/u and were normalised. Several words in the verse may be misread due to the faded print and are not marked.
